claims.claim: Visa and Mastercard primarily operate payment networks; the logo generally identifies the network rather than the lender.
Issuing banks generally issue credit cards, extend credit and bear associated lending risk.
In the simplified four-party model, merchant acquirers/processors connect the merchant to a network; requests reach the issuer and responses return. Issuers generally decide authorization.
Network revenue includes processing and cross-border services. The toll-road comparison is an analogy, not a statement that all fees are per swipe or identical across networks.
Total merchant charges are not entirely network revenue. Interchange is generally paid by acquirers to issuers; merchant providers also earn fees.
Payment networks can bear settlement/counterparty exposures; avoiding consumer lending does not mean no credit exposure or no risk.
